{{Color box|{{party color|One Cebu}}|border=darkgray}} [[One Cebu|1CEBU]] | blank2_name = Congressional bloc | blank2_info = Majority }} '''Cebu's 2nd congressional district''' is one of the seven [[congressional districts of the Philippines]] in the province of [[Cebu]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1916 and earlier in the [[Philippine Assembly]] from 1907 to 1916.{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 20, 2020 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} The district consists of the southern Cebu municipalities of [[Alcoy, Cebu|Alcoy]], [[Argao]], [[Boljoon]], [[Dalaguete]], [[Oslob, Cebu|Oslob]], [[Samboan]] and [[Santander, Cebu|Santander]]. It is currently represented in the [[19th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Edsel Galeos]] of the [[Lakas–CMD]] (Lakas) and [[One Cebu]] (1CEBU).{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 22, 2023}} The district served as an electoral district in the [[Philippine Constitutional Convention of 1934|1934 Constitutional Convention]], electing two delegates, and in the [[Philippine Constitutional Convention of 1971|1971 Constitutional Convention]], electing four delegates.{{Cite PH act|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/28/15525|chamber=Act|number=4125|date=May 26, 1934|title=An Act to Provide for the Election and Holding of the Constitutional Convention Authorized by the Act of the Congress of the United States of March Twenty-Fourth, Nineteen Hundred and Thirty-Four, Appropriate Funds Therefor, and for Other Purposes}}{{Cite PH act|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/14108|chamber=RA|number=6132|date=August 24, 1970|title=An Act Implementing Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Two as Amended by Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Four of the Congress of the Philippines Calling for a Constitutional Convention, Providing for Proportional Representation Therein and Other Details Relating to the Election of Delegates to and the Holding of the Constitutional Convention, Repealing for the Purpose Republic Act Four Thousand Nine Hundred Fourteen, and for Other Purposes}} Prior to its second dissolution in 1972, the district encompassed the cities of [[Cebu City|Cebu]], [[Lapu-Lapu City|Lapu-Lapu]], and [[Mandaue]], and the eastern municipalities of [[Compostela, Cebu|Compostela]], [[Consolacion, Cebu|Consolacion]], [[Cordova, Cebu|Cordova]], and [[Liloan, Cebu|Liloan]]. The southwestern municipalities of [[Alcantara, Cebu|Alcantara]], [[Argao]], [[Badian, Cebu|Badian]], [[Dumanjug]], [[Ginatilan]], [[Malabuyoc]], [[Moalboal]], and [[Ronda, Cebu|Ronda]] belonged to the district from 1987 until they were reapportioned to the re-created [[Cebu's 7th congressional district|seventh district]] in 2016. {{clear}} == List of members representing the district == === Philippine Assembly (1907–1916) === {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" ! width="100px" | Portrait ! width="135px" | Member
